hook_text: A family is building a rondavel. Thatch, tin or tiles? There is no single right answer — but there is a smart way to decide.
clip_script: Thatch: cheap if the grass grows nearby, cool in summer, warm in winter, silent in a storm. But it burns, and it must be replaced every couple of decades. Tin, corrugated iron: cheap, quick, fireproof, and you can catch rainwater off it. But without a ceiling the room bakes in summer and freezes in winter, and rain sounds like drums. Clay tiles: long-lasting, fireproof, good-looking. But heavy and expensive. Properties tell you what can work. Then cost, looks, feel, how long it lasts and safety decide what is best. That is why wires are copper, not gold, and why so many roofs in hot places are painted white: it bounces the sunlight away. Smart choices weigh it all up.
visual_style: Whiteboard rondavel with three roof options swapping in; a scorecard filling with ticks and crosses; a white roof reflecting Sun arrows.
pacing: Three quick roof pitches, a scorecard moment, a confident finish.
